```{r setup, include=FALSE}
projection_data <- Sys.getenv("NYC_PROJ_DIR")
if (nzchar(projection_data)) sf::sf_proj_search_paths(projection_data)
source("scripts/analysis.R")
source("scripts/widgets.R")
source("module_A/housing_analysis.R")
source("module_A/visualizations.R")
source("module_B/visualizations.R")
source("module_C/visualizations.R")
source("module_D/visualizations.R")
source("module_E/visualizations.R")
nyc <- load_analysis()
b1_medians <- nyc$tr[borough %in% c("Bronx", "Manhattan") & is.finite(night_rate),
  .(median_rate = median(night_rate)), by = borough]
b2_days <- calendar[, .(days = .N), by = .(weekend = weekday >= 6L)]
b2_residential <- period_data(nyc, "Residential")[, .(calls = sum(calls)),
  by = .(weekend = weekday >= 6L, hour)]
b2_residential[b2_days, daily := calls / i.days, on = "weekend"]
b2_peaks <- b2_residential[order(-daily, hour), .SD[1L], by = weekend]
b3 <- noise_monthly_summary(nyc$time)
housing <- housing_data(nyc$tr)
housing_charts <- housing_widgets(nyc, housing)
housing_author <- "王韬涵 / 2430026200"
charts <- list(housing_charts, noise_widgets(nyc, b3), safety_widgets(nyc),
               tradeoff_widgets(nyc), profile_widgets(nyc))
stopifnot(identical(lengths(charts), c(7L, 8L, 8L, 6L, 10L)))
dp <- attr(charts[[4]], "summary")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
qa_noise <- nyc$audit[source == "311 noise"]
qa_nypd <- nyc$audit[source == "NYPD"]
rent_mid <- median(nyc$tr$rent, na.rm = TRUE)
num_profiles <- nrow(nyc$profile)
ex <- nyc$examples
quad_n <- nyc$profile[quad == quad_labels[4], .N]
boro_rent <- nyc$tr[!is.na(rent), .(median_rent = median(as.numeric(rent))), by = borough][order(-median_rent)]
```

Row

### A1 · Where rents are higher

<p class="a-author">Presenter · `r htmltools::htmlEscape(housing_author)`</p>

`r show_n(nrow(housing$rent))` of `r show_n(nrow(nyc$tr))` NYC census tracts have a published ACS rent estimate. Across those tracts, the median is **`r show_dollar(median(housing$rent$rent))` per month**.

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r a-rent-map}
housing_charts$rent_map
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">The median of tract rent estimates is <strong>`r show_dollar(housing$borough_rents[borough == "Manhattan", median_rent])` in Manhattan</strong> and <strong>`r show_dollar(housing$borough_rents[borough == "Bronx", median_rent])` in the Bronx</strong>. Color intensity shows fixed monthly rent bands. Hover for tract estimates. Grey indicates missing rent.</p>

### A1 · How rent varies with household income

Among `r show_n(housing$income_exact_n)` tracts with both figures below their upper categories, the citywide Spearman correlation is **`r sprintf("%.2f", housing$income_rho)`**. It ranges from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(housing$income_stats$rho))` in `r housing$income_stats[which.min(rho), borough]` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(housing$income_stats$rho))` in `r housing$income_stats[which.max(rho), borough]`.

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r a-income-rent}
housing_charts$income_rent
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">One point per tract. Borough color is categorical. Open diamonds flag an ACS upper category for either estimate. Click the legend to focus on a borough. Median household income covers all households in the tract.</p>

Row
------------------------------------------

### A2 · Budget coverage across thresholds

At **$1,750**, Brooklyn covers `r show_pct(housing$coverage[budget == 1750 & borough == "Brooklyn", share])` of eligible tracts and Queens covers `r show_pct(housing$coverage[budget == 1750 & borough == "Queens", share])`. At **$2,250**, their shares are `r show_pct(housing$coverage[budget == 2250 & borough == "Brooklyn", share])` and `r show_pct(housing$coverage[budget == 2250 & borough == "Queens", share])`.

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r a-coverage-curve}
housing_charts$coverage
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">The steps rise at the exact published rent estimates. The dotted line follows the selected budget. Denominators include all tracts with a published rent in each borough. The $3,500+ category stays above every available budget.</p>

### A2 · Five boroughs at the same budget

<div class="a-budget-control">
  <label for="a-budget">Monthly rent ceiling <output id="a-budget-value" for="a-budget">$2,000</output></label>
  <input id="a-budget" type="range" min="1000" max="3450" step="50" value="2000" />
  <div class="nyc-controls" id="a-budget-presets"><button type="button" value="1750">$1,750</button><button type="button" value="2000">$2,000</button><button type="button" value="2250">$2,250</button></div>
  <p id="a-budget-status" role="status">`r show_n(housing$coverage[budget == 2000, sum(count)])` eligible tracts citywide within budget</p>
</div>

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r a-budget-bars}
housing_charts$budget_bar
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">Each tract receives equal weight. Coverage describes the share of tract medians at or below the ceiling. Use it to screen areas by historical rents. Current listings and rental-unit inventories require separate data.</p>

Row
------------------------------------------

### A3 · Rent and rent burden

Among **`r show_n(nrow(housing$burden))` tracts**, `r show_n(housing$burden[contrast == housing$sides[1], .N])` are in the lower-rent, higher-burden corner and `r show_n(housing$burden[contrast == housing$sides[2], .N])` are in the opposite corner.

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r a-burden-scatter}
housing_charts$burden_scatter
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">The shaded corners combine the bottom and top quarters of the two citywide rank scales. Axes show the original values. Ringed points mark the Manhattan cases below. Rent burden is the share of renter households spending at least 30% of income on gross rent among those with a computable ratio.</p>

### A3 · Largest gaps between the two ranks

The gap is burden percentile less rent percentile. The bars show the four strongest exact-rent examples from each opposite corner.

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r a-rank-gaps}
housing_charts$rank_gap
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">Positive values mean burden ranks higher. Both ranks use the same eligible tracts and average ties. Spearman’s rho is `r sprintf("%.2f", housing$burden_rho)` for the full sample and `r sprintf("%.2f", housing$burden_rho_exact)` after excluding $3,500+ rents.</p>

Row
------------------------------------------

### A3 · Two Manhattan tracts

::: {.a-case-layout}

::: {.nyc-viz .a-case-viz}

```{r a-case-composition}
housing_charts$case_composition
```

:::

::: {.a-case-copy}

**East Harlem (North), tract 021000**
`r show_rent(housing$cases$rent[1])` median monthly rent and **`r show_pct(housing$cases$burden_rate[1])`** rent burden among `r show_n(housing$cases$computable[1])` computable renter households.

**East Village, tract 002202**
`r show_rent(housing$cases$rent[2])` median monthly rent and **`r show_pct(housing$cases$burden_rate[2])`** rent burden among `r show_n(housing$cases$computable[2])` computable renter households.

The share spending 50% or more of income on rent was `r show_pct(housing$case_bands$severe[1] / housing$case_bands$computable[1])` in the East Harlem tract and `r show_pct(housing$case_bands$severe[2] / housing$case_bands$computable[2])` in the East Village tract.

:::

:::

<details class="nyc-audit">
  <summary>Data and methods</summary>
  <p>The group joined ACS 2020–2024 five-year estimates to 2020 NYC census tract boundaries by GEOID after treating negative Census special codes as missing. A1 has `r show_n(nrow(housing$rent))` tracts with rent and `r show_n(nrow(housing$income))` with both rent and income. Its correlations exclude estimates in either ACS upper category. A2 uses all tracts with rent, including top-coded estimates in the denominator. A3 requires a rent estimate, a valid burden rate and at least 50 renter households with a computable ratio.</p>
  <p>Estimates describe tracts and renter households during the ACS period. Tract estimates have sampling uncertainty. The two Manhattan cases illustrate the opposite combinations and have at least 500 computable renter households each.</p>
</details>

<p class="nyc-note"><a href="https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/data/summary-file.2024.html">U.S. Census ACS 2020–2024</a> · <a href="https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/groups/B25064.html">Gross rent</a> · <a href="https://api.census.gov/data/2024/acs/acs5/groups/B25070.html">Rent-to-income bands</a>.</p>

<div class="nyc-task-notes" id="b1-task-notes">

</div>

Rent & Noise {#tradeoffs data-orientation=rows}

Row
------------------------------------------

### D1 · Rent and night reporting quadrants

<p>Do higher-rent tracts consistently have fewer night reports?</p>

<p><strong>`r show_n(quad_n)` of `r show_n(num_profiles)`</strong> eligible tracts have both rent and night reporting at or above the respective medians.</p>

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r chart-4-1}
charts[[4]][[1]]
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">Lines mark medians across tracts with all profile fields available. Click a tract to locate it on the map.</p>

```{r rent-sensitivity, results='asis'}
s <- copy(nyc$tradeoff_check)
s[, `:=`(tracts = show_n(tracts), correlation = sprintf("%.3f", correlation), high_high = show_pct(high_high))]
setnames(s, c("Sample", "Tracts", "Spearman ρ", "At/above both medians"))
htmltools::tags$details(class = "nyc-audit", id = "rent-sensitivity",
  htmltools::tags$summary("Check $3,500+ rents and unusually high report rates"),
  htmltools::tags$p("We recalculate the rank correlation between rent and night requests and the share at or above both sample medians. The reporting filter excludes a tract if either its night request rate or its NYPD complaint rate exceeds the original eligible sample's 99th percentile for that measure."),
  htmltools::HTML(knitr::kable(s, format = "html")),
  htmltools::tags$p("Use the association to describe tract-level patterns. Individual decisions and typical noise exposure require different measurements.")
)
```

### D2 · How far apart can two similar-rent tracts be?

<p>Every pair of tracts inside one borough whose median gross rent differs by $100 or less, compared on three outcomes at once.</p>

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r chart-4-3}
charts[[4]][[3]]
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">`r show_n(dp$n_pairs)` pairs across `r show_n(dp$tracts)` tracts. Half of the pairs differ by at most `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$night_median)` late-night requests per 1,000 residents, but the worst tenth differ by `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$night_p90)` or more. Top-coded rents, where ACS reports only "$3,500 or more", are excluded because the true gap is unknown.</p>

### D2 · Does the rent window change the answer?

<p>Repeat the comparison with a $50 and a $150 window.</p>

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r chart-4-4}
charts[[4]][[4]]
```

:::

<p class="nyc-note">The three curves nearly coincide. The median night-report gap is `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$thresholds[threshold == 50, night_median])`, `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$thresholds[threshold == 100, night_median])` and `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$thresholds[threshold == 150, night_median])` at the three windows, and the 90th percentile moves from `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$thresholds[threshold == 50, night_p90])` to `r sprintf("%.1f", dp$thresholds[threshold == 150, night_p90])`. The rent window is not what drives the result.</p>

### E2 · Blurry boundary pair diagnostic

<p>Which profile pairs share the most overlapping transition tracts?</p>

::: {.nyc-viz}

```{r chart-5-6}

```

:::

<p class="nyc-note"><strong>Readout:</strong> Overlap concentrates between P2 &lt;-&gt; P3 (140 tracts, 36.0% of the blurry zone) and P1 &lt;-&gt; P3 (113 tracts), whereas P2 &lt;-&gt; P4 has only 5 boundary tracts.</p>

```{r group-sensitivity, results='asis'}
model_check <- copy(nyc$model_check)
model_check[, mean_width := sprintf("%.3f", mean_width)]
setnames(model_check, c("Groups (K)", "Mean silhouette"))
stability <- copy(nyc$stability_check)
stability[, `:=`(tracts = show_n(tracts), agreement = sprintf("%.3f", agreement))]
setnames(stability, c("Refit sample", "Tracts", "Adjusted Rand index"))
htmltools::tags$details(class = "nyc-audit", id = "group-sensitivity",
  htmltools::tags$summary("Model settings, separation and sensitivity"),
  htmltools::tags$p("The page uses four groups for exploratory comparison. K-means standardizes rent (with the $3,500+ category represented at its published lower bound) and the log1p transforms of night requests, NYPD complaints, rail distance and density. Each fit uses seed 4073, 25 starts and up to 100 iterations. Population density supplies context for the profiles."),
  htmltools::HTML(knitr::kable(model_check, format = "html")),
  htmltools::tags$p("The observed silhouette widths indicate substantial overlap. We also re-standardize and refit the four-group model after the exclusions in Rent & Noise. The adjusted Rand index compares the baseline and refitted group assignments for the retained tracts. A value of 1 means the assignments agree, and 0 means chance-level agreement."),
  htmltools::HTML(knitr::kable(stability, format = "html"))
)
```

```{r interactivity, results='asis'}
types <- c("All types", noise_types)
hour_data <- setNames(lapply(types, function(x) {
  t <- period_data(nyc, x)
  list(rate = matrix(t$rate, nrow = 7L, byrow = TRUE),
       counts = matrix(t$calls, nrow = 7L, byrow = TRUE))
}), types)
weights <- calendar[, .N, by = weekday][match(1:7, weekday), N]
sensitivity <- nyc$profile[, .(GEOID, label, borough, cost, quiet, reports, rail, rent, night_rate, nypd_rate, station_m)]
link_labels <- nyc$profile[, .(label, GEOID, quad, cluster)]
boro_med_map <- setNames(as.list(boro_rent$median_rent), boro_rent$borough)
payload <- jsonlite::toJSON(list(noise = hour_data, days = weights, profiles = sensitivity,
                                 links = link_labels, colors = as.list(boro_colors),
                                 boro_med = boro_med_map), auto_unbox = TRUE)
cat("\n```{=html}\n<script type='application/json' id='nyc-payload'>", payload, "</script>\n<script>\n",
    paste(readLines("scripts/dashboard.js", warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"), "\n</script>\n```\n", sep = "")
```
